CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management and assessment of lower extremity edema post-furosemide initiation.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit regarding his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and the management of bilateral lower extremity edema. He reports a modest improvement in his respiratory symptoms since his last visit. The patient states that he has been using his albuterol inhaler less frequently, averaging once daily, and he continues to find the fluticasone/salmeterol inhaler effective in managing his baseline symptoms. Notably, there have been no exacerbations since his last appointment.
Mr. Fairfax mentions that while his sleep quality has remained stable, he occasionally experiences mild wheezing, particularly during cold mornings. He denies any episodes of nocturnal dyspnea or significant cough.
Concerning his leg swelling, Mr. Fairfax reports that since starting furosemide, the edema has decreased to 1+ pitting. He expresses satisfaction with this improvement, noting that he has adhered to dietary sodium restrictions and has continued to elevate his legs. He denies any associated symptoms such as pain, redness, or warmth in the extremities, and he has not experienced chest pain or shortness of breath.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + stable energy levels, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - - cough, - sputum production, + mild wheezing, - dyspnea on exertion, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily 4. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain 5. Furosemide 20 mg daily
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.4F, HR 76, BP 124/72, RR 18, O2 sat 96% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.1, Hgb 13.8, Hct 40.5, Plt 215 2. BMP: Na 139, K 4.2, Cl 101, CO2 27, BUN 12, Cr 0.8, Glucose 95 3. BNP: 390 (decreased from previous visit) 4. CXR: Stable hyperinflation of lungs, no acute changes.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Continue current inhaler regimen. Patient education reinforced regarding recognizing early signs of exacerbation and the importance of adherence to inhaler use. Schedule follow-up in 2 months or sooner if symptoms worsen. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains well-controlled. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: Continue furosemide 20 mg daily given the positive response. Monitor weight and sodium intake closely. Reassess in 1 month. 4. Follow up with pulmonary medicine for ongoing management.
Patient education emphasized regarding fluid management strategies and the importance of maintaining a heart-healthy diet.
